pa_south_buttress_linoy_buttress.blurb: The longest and tallest face at Dauphin Narrows, a cliff on Second Mountain above the Susquehanna north of Harrisburg. Seventeen mostly trad lines run from easy fifth-class up through a few 5.10s to a single 5.11, plus a couple of multi-pitch routes and one aid line. This is adventure climbing rather than a polished crag: moves can be awkward, some routes are run out, the rock is loose in places, and descents often mean several rappels, so bring a helmet, a standard rack and spare cord for anchors. The walk from the road is short but the trail to the base is steep, and traffic noise makes talking hard.
pa_south_buttress_linoy_buttress.parking_note: Drive to the end of Cemetery Road and leave the car in the pull-off there.

pa_d_tenuous_odyssey_sector.blurb: A mid-range sector on the southern half of Safe Harbor, a string of cliffs beside the Enola Low Grade rail trail above the Susquehanna. It is the third group of routes you meet walking north from the Green Hill Road tunnel, wedged between the Electric Co. and Machismo sectors. Sixteen routes: mostly bolted single pitches, a handful of trad lines and one top-rope, from easy fives through a solid middle of 5.9 to 5.11, with a lone 5.13. The south end generally offers low-angle rock with good friction and the odd steeper line, so it suits climbers working through the moderate grades.
pa_d_tenuous_odyssey_sector.parking_note: Leave the car on Green Hill Road just before or after the tunnel; there is room for plenty of vehicles, though they have to turn around to get out.

pa_8_castellan.blurb: A modest trad crag on the cliffs over the west bank of the Susquehanna in York County, within Susquehanna Riverlands State Park. Sixteen routes on quartzite, all protected with your own gear: slabs, corners and cracks, with a few lines split across lower, mid and upper gullies. Grades start at fourth class and are mostly 5.5 to 5.9, topping out around 5.10. It is shorter than its upriver neighbours, and traffic is light enough that rock can be loose and vegetation thick, so wear a helmet and look over a line before leading it. Some climbs are easier to top-rope after leading them to set the rope.

pa_4_50_cemetery_wall.blurb: A steep, densely packed sport wall about 140 feet tall, found at mile 4.5 of the Enola Low Grade rail trail in the northern half of Safe Harbor. Sixteen routes, nearly all bolted, with one aid line; the bulk sit between 5.11 and 5.12, backed by a few 5.9s and a 5.10 and one 5.13, so it rewards climbers already comfortable in the 5.11 range. Lines in the northern section run steeper and more spread out than the southern end and have a Gunks-like feel. Bring a 60 metre rope and a good selection of quickdraws; The Nose goes in two pitches.

pa_i_sun_wall_long_slabs.blurb: A sport wall in the old Birdsboro Quarry, reached by a trail that drops toward the reservoir and branches off through the woods. All sixteen routes are bolted, mostly in the 5.9 to 5.11 range with a couple of easier lines around 5.7 and 5.8, so it works well for steady cragging in the lower and middle grades. A few of the routes are long slabs that run to two true pitches, which means two rappels to get down. The rock is diabase, quarry-cut and uneven in quality, and a single 60 metre rope handles most lines.
